q: What does Amazon S3 stand for?

exp.a: Correct. Amazon S3 stands for Simple Storage Service.
exp.b: Incorrect. S3 does not stand for Secure Storage Service.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 does not stand for Scalable Storage System.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 does not stand for Simple System Storage.

q: What is the maximum size of a single object that can be stored in Amazon S3?

exp.a: Incorrect. 5 GB is the maximum size for a single PUT operation, not the maximum object size.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum size of a single object in S3 is 5 TB (5 terabytes).
exp.c: Incorrect. The limit is 5 TB, not 10 TB.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a 5 TB limit per object, though total storage is virtually unlimited.

q: What is the maximum size of a single PUT upload in Amazon S3?

exp.a: Incorrect. 5 MB is not the limit for a single PUT; it is the minimum part size for multipart upload.
exp.b: Incorrect. AWS recommends multipart upload for objects over 100 MB, but the PUT limit is 5 GB.
exp.c: Correct. A single PUT operation can upload an object up to 5 GB in size.
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 TB is the maximum object size, not the single PUT limit.

q: Amazon S3 bucket names must be globally unique across which scope?

opts.a: Within the same AWS account only
opts.b: Within the same AWS Region only
opts.c: Across all existing AWS accounts worldwide

exp.a: Incorrect. Bucket names must be unique across all AWS accounts, not just one account.
exp.b: Incorrect. Bucket names are globally unique, not just within a region.
exp.c: Correct. S3 bucket names must be globally unique across all AWS accounts worldwide.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 is not tied to a VPC; bucket names are globally unique.

q: Which S3 storage class is designed for frequently accessed data?

exp.a: Correct. S3 Standard is designed for frequently accessed data with low latency and high throughput.
exp.b: Incorrect. S3 Standard-IA (Infrequent Access) is for data accessed less frequently.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 One Zone-IA is for infrequently accessed data stored in a single AZ.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 Glacier is designed for long-term archival storage.

q: How many Availability Zones does S3 Standard replicate data across?

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in 1 AZ, not S3 Standard.
exp.b: Incorrect. S3 Standard replicates across a minimum of 3 AZs.
exp.c: Correct. S3 Standard automatically replicates data across a minimum of 3 Availability Zones.
exp.d: Incorrect. The minimum is 3 AZs, not necessarily 5.

q: What is the durability guarantee of Amazon S3 Standard?

exp.a: Incorrect. 99.9% is too low; that relates to availability SLA for some classes.
exp.b: Incorrect. 99.99% is the availability SLA for S3 Standard, not durability.
exp.c: Correct. S3 Standard provides 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability.
exp.d: Incorrect. The durability is 11 nines, not 7 nines.

q: What is the availability SLA for S3 Standard?

exp.a: Incorrect. 99% availability is for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
exp.b: Incorrect. 99.5% availability applies to S3 One Zone-IA.
exp.c: Incorrect. 99.9% availability applies to S3 Standard-IA and S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
exp.d: Correct. S3 Standard is designed for 99.99% availability.

q: Which S3 storage class stores data in only one Availability Zone?

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 Standard replicates across 3+ AZs.
exp.b: Incorrect. S3 Standard-IA also replicates across 3+ AZs.
exp.c: Correct. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, reducing cost.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 Glacier Deep Archive replicates across 3+ AZs.

q: What is the minimum storage duration charge for S3 Standard-IA?

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 Standard has no minimum storage duration, but Standard-IA does.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Standard-IA has a minimum storage duration charge of 30 days.
exp.c: Incorrect. 90 days is the minimum for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
exp.d: Incorrect. 180 days is the minimum for S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

q: What is the minimum storage duration charge for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval?

exp.a: Incorrect. 30 days is the minimum for S3 Standard-IA and One Zone-IA.
exp.b: Incorrect. There is no S3 class with a 60-day minimum duration.
exp.c: Correct. S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval has a minimum storage duration charge of 90 days.
exp.d: Incorrect. 180 days is the minimum for S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

q: What is the minimum storage duration charge for S3 Glacier Deep Archive?

exp.a: Incorrect. 30 days applies to S3 Standard-IA.
exp.b: Incorrect. 90 days applies to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
exp.c: Correct. S3 Glacier Deep Archive has a minimum storage duration charge of 180 days.
exp.d: Incorrect. No S3 class has a 365-day minimum duration charge.

q: What is the minimum object size charge for S3 Standard-IA?

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 Standard has no minimum object size charge, but IA classes do.
exp.b: Incorrect. 64 KB is not the correct minimum for Standard-IA.
exp.c: Correct. S3 Standard-IA has a minimum billable object size of 128 KB.
exp.d: Incorrect. The minimum is 128 KB, not 256 KB.

q: Which feature allows you to automatically move objects between S3 storage classes based on rules?

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 Replication copies objects to another bucket, not between storage classes.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Lifecycle Policies allow automatic transitions between storage classes and object expiration.
exp.c: Incorrect. Versioning keeps multiple versions of objects but doesn't move them between classes.
exp.d: Incorrect. Event Notifications trigger actions on events, not storage class transitions.

q: What is S3 Versioning used for?

opts.b: To keep multiple variants of an object in the same bucket

exp.a: Incorrect. Encryption at rest is handled by SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, or SSE-C.
exp.b: Correct. Versioning preserves, retrieves, and restores every version of every object in a bucket.
exp.c: Incorrect. Cross-region replication handles replication, not versioning alone.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 does not automatically compress objects; versioning keeps multiple versions.

q: When versioning is enabled and an object is deleted, what does S3 create?

exp.a: Incorrect. DynamoDB is not involved in S3 versioning.
exp.b: Correct. When versioning is enabled, deleting an object creates a delete marker instead of permanently removing it.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudTrail logs the API call but S3 itself creates a delete marker.
exp.d: Incorrect. With versioning enabled, objects are not permanently deleted unless a specific version ID is used.

q: Which S3 encryption method uses keys managed entirely by AWS without customer involvement?

exp.a: Incorrect. SSE-C requires the customer to provide and manage their own encryption keys.
exp.b: Incorrect. SSE-KMS uses AWS KMS keys which can be customer-managed or AWS-managed, but still involve KMS.
exp.c: Correct. SSE-S3 uses keys managed entirely by AWS S3 with no customer key management required.
exp.d: Incorrect. Client-side encryption is performed by the client before uploading.

q: Which S3 encryption method allows you to use AWS KMS customer managed keys (CMKs) for envelope encryption?

exp.a: Incorrect. SSE-S3 uses Amazon S3-managed keys, not KMS CMKs.
exp.b: Correct. SSE-KMS uses AWS KMS customer managed keys and provides envelope encryption with audit trail via CloudTrail.
exp.c: Incorrect. SSE-C uses customer-provided keys sent with each request.
exp.d: Incorrect. TLS encrypts data in transit, not at rest.

q: With SSE-C encryption, who is responsible for managing the encryption keys?

exp.a: Incorrect. SSE-S3 is where AWS S3 manages the keys.
exp.b: Incorrect. SSE-KMS is where KMS manages the keys.
exp.c: Correct. With SSE-C, the customer provides and manages the encryption keys with each request.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudHSM can be used separately but SSE-C means customer-provided keys.

q: What protocol must be used when uploading objects with SSE-C?

exp.a: Incorrect. HTTP is not allowed for SSE-C because the key would be sent unencrypted.
exp.b: Correct. HTTPS is mandatory for SSE-C to protect the encryption key in transit.
exp.c: Incorrect. FTP is not a supported S3 protocol for this purpose.
exp.d: Incorrect. SFTP is available via AWS Transfer Family but SSE-C specifically requires HTTPS for S3 API calls.

q: What is the default encryption behavior for new S3 buckets as of January 2023?

opts.a: No encryption is applied by default

exp.a: Incorrect. Since January 2023, AWS applies encryption by default.
exp.b: Incorrect. SSE-KMS is not the default; it must be configured explicitly.
exp.c: Correct. As of January 2023, all new objects in S3 are encrypted with SSE-S3 (AES-256) by default.
exp.d: Incorrect. Client-side encryption is not a default; server-side SSE-S3 is.

q: Which S3 feature allows you to replicate objects across different AWS Regions?

exp.a: Incorrect. SRR replicates within the same region, not across regions.
exp.b: Correct. Cross-Region Replication (CRR) replicates objects across different AWS Regions.
exp.c: Incorrect. Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads via CloudFront edge locations.
exp.d: Incorrect. Batch Operations performs bulk operations on existing objects.

q: What is a prerequisite for enabling S3 Replication (CRR or SRR)?

opts.b: Versioning must be enabled on both source and destination buckets
opts.c: The buckets must be in the same AWS account
opts.d: Objects must be less than 1 GB

exp.a: Incorrect. Encryption can be enabled; replication works with encrypted objects.
exp.b: Correct. Versioning must be enabled on both the source and destination buckets for replication.
exp.c: Incorrect. Replication can work across different AWS accounts.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is no 1 GB size restriction for replication.

q: Which S3 feature speeds up long-distance data transfers to S3 using AWS edge locations?

exp.a: Incorrect. CRR replicates data between buckets, not for speeding uploads.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront edge locations to accelerate uploads over long distances.
exp.c: Incorrect. Multipart Upload splits large files into parts but doesn't use edge locations.
exp.d: Incorrect. Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection, not an S3-specific feature.

q: AWS recommends using S3 Multipart Upload for files larger than what size?

exp.a: Incorrect. 5 MB is the minimum part size, not the recommended threshold.
exp.b: Correct. AWS recommends using Multipart Upload for objects larger than 100 MB.
exp.c: Incorrect. The recommendation is 100 MB, not 1 GB.
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 GB is the maximum single PUT size, and multipart is mandatory above this.

q: What is the maximum number of parts allowed in a single S3 Multipart Upload?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 1,000 parts.
exp.b: Incorrect. 5,000 is the listing limit for ListParts, not the maximum number of parts.
exp.c: Correct. S3 Multipart Upload supports up to 10,000 parts.
exp.d: Incorrect. The maximum is 10,000 parts, not 100,000.

q: What is S3 Object Lock used for?

opts.b: Preventing objects from being deleted or overwritten for a fixed period (WORM model)
opts.d: Restricting access to a single IAM user

exp.a: Incorrect. Encryption is handled by SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, or SSE-C.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Object Lock provides Write Once Read Many (WORM) protection to prevent deletion or modification.
exp.c: Incorrect. Bucket policies are managed via IAM and bucket policy settings.
exp.d: Incorrect. Access control is managed through IAM policies and bucket policies.

q: Which S3 Object Lock retention mode allows a user with special permissions to delete or overwrite a protected object?

exp.a: Incorrect. Compliance mode does not allow anyone, including root, to delete or modify the object during retention.
exp.b: Correct. Governance mode allows users with the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission to remove the lock.
exp.c: Incorrect. Legal Hold is not a retention mode; it can be placed/removed by users with permission but doesn't have a retention period.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is no 'Standard mode' in S3 Object Lock.

q: In S3 Object Lock Compliance mode, who can delete a protected object before the retention period expires?

opts.b: Any IAM user with admin permissions
opts.c: No one, not even the root account

exp.a: Incorrect. Even the root user cannot override Compliance mode retention.
exp.b: Incorrect. No IAM user regardless of permissions can delete the object.
exp.c: Correct. In Compliance mode, no one can delete or overwrite the object until the retention period expires.
exp.d: Incorrect. AWS Support also cannot override Compliance mode.

q: What is an S3 presigned URL used for?

opts.b: Granting temporary access to a private object via a time-limited URL

exp.a: Incorrect. Presigned URLs are temporary and do not make buckets permanently public.
exp.b: Correct. Presigned URLs grant temporary, time-limited access to private S3 objects.
exp.c: Incorrect. Encryption is separate from presigned URLs.
exp.d: Incorrect. Versioning is a bucket-level setting, not related to presigned URLs.

q: What is the maximum expiration time for an S3 presigned URL generated using IAM credentials (long-term)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 hour is the max when using STS temporary credentials with a 1-hour session.
exp.b: Incorrect. 6 hours is the max when using STS with a 6-hour session limit.
exp.c: Correct. Presigned URLs generated with IAM user long-term credentials can be valid up to 7 days (604800 seconds).
exp.d: Incorrect. 30 days exceeds the maximum allowed expiration.

q: Which S3 feature allows hosting a static website?

exp.a: Incorrect. Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads, not website hosting.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Static Website Hosting allows you to host static web content directly from an S3 bucket.
exp.c: Incorrect. Glacier is for archival, not website hosting.
exp.d: Incorrect. Replication copies data between buckets.

q: When using S3 static website hosting, what is the format of the website endpoint?

exp.a: Incorrect. This is the REST API endpoint, not the website endpoint.
exp.b: Correct. The S3 website endpoint format is http://bucket-name.s3-website-region.amazonaws.com (or s3-website.region).
exp.c: Incorrect. This would be a CloudFront distribution URL.
exp.d: Incorrect. EC2 endpoints are not related to S3 website hosting.

q: What must be configured to allow public read access for S3 static website hosting?

opts.b: Disable Block Public Access settings and add a bucket policy allowing public read

exp.a: Incorrect. Versioning is not required for public website access.
exp.b: Correct. You must disable Block Public Access settings and attach a bucket policy granting s3:GetObject to everyone (*).
exp.c: Incorrect. Encryption is not required and does not grant public access.
exp.d: Incorrect. CORS is for cross-origin requests, not for granting public read access.

q: What is S3 CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) used for?

opts.b: Allowing web browsers to make requests to S3 from a different origin domain
opts.d: Restricting access to specific IP addresses

exp.a: Incorrect. CORS is not related to encryption.
exp.b: Correct. CORS configuration allows web browsers to make cross-origin requests to S3 from different domains.
exp.c: Incorrect. Compression is not the purpose of CORS.
exp.d: Incorrect. IP restrictions are handled via bucket policies, not CORS.

q: What is S3 Select used for?

opts.a: Selecting which storage class to use
opts.b: Retrieving a subset of data from an object using SQL-like expressions

exp.a: Incorrect. Storage class selection is done via lifecycle policies or at upload time.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Select allows you to use simple SQL expressions to retrieve only the needed subset of data from an object (CSV, JSON, Parquet).
exp.c: Incorrect. Replication rules handle object selection for replication.
exp.d: Incorrect. Encryption method selection is a configuration choice, not related to S3 Select.

q: Which AWS service can be used to query S3 data in-place using standard SQL without loading it into a database?

exp.a: Incorrect. RDS is a managed relational database, not for querying S3 directly.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon Athena is a serverless query service that uses SQL to analyze data directly in S3.
exp.c: Incorrect. DynamoDB is a NoSQL database, not for querying S3.
exp.d: Incorrect. ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service.

q: Which S3 storage class provides instant retrieval with lower cost for infrequently accessed data?

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 Standard is for frequently accessed data.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval provides millisecond access for data accessed once per quarter, at lower cost than Standard-IA.
exp.c: Incorrect. Glacier Flexible Retrieval has retrieval times from minutes to hours.
exp.d: Incorrect. Glacier Deep Archive has retrieval times of 12-48 hours.

q: What are the retrieval options available for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval?

opts.b: Expedited (1-5 min), Standard (3-5 hours), Bulk (5-12 hours)

exp.a: Incorrect. Instant retrieval is for S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval class.
exp.b: Correct. Glacier Flexible Retrieval offers Expedited (1-5 min), Standard (3-5 hours), and Bulk (5-12 hours) options.
exp.c: Incorrect. These are retrieval times for Glacier Deep Archive.
exp.d: Incorrect. There are no options called 'Real-time and Batch' in S3 Glacier.

q: What are the retrieval times for S3 Glacier Deep Archive?

exp.a: Incorrect. These are the retrieval times for Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
exp.b: Correct. Glacier Deep Archive has Standard retrieval of 12 hours and Bulk retrieval of 48 hours.
exp.c: Incorrect. Glacier Deep Archive does not provide instant access.
exp.d: Incorrect. These times are too short for Deep Archive.

q: Which S3 storage class automatically moves objects between access tiers based on access patterns?

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 Standard does not automatically tier objects.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between Frequent, Infrequent, Archive Instant, Archive, and Deep Archive tiers based on usage patterns.
exp.c: Incorrect. Standard-IA is a fixed storage class.
exp.d: Incorrect. Glacier Flexible Retrieval is a fixed archival class.

q: How many access tiers does S3 Intelligent-Tiering support?

exp.a: Incorrect. Intelligent-Tiering has more than 2 tiers.
exp.b: Incorrect. It has more than 3 tiers.
exp.c: Correct. S3 Intelligent-Tiering has 5 tiers: Frequent Access, Infrequent Access (30 days), Archive Instant Access (90 days), Archive Access (optional, 90 days), and Deep Archive Access (optional, 180 days).
exp.d: Incorrect. There are 5 tiers, not 7.

q: What is the consistency model for Amazon S3 as of December 2020?

opts.b: Strong read-after-write consistency for all operations
opts.d: Eventual consistency for GETs, strong for DELETEs

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 previously had eventual consistency for overwrite PUTs and DELETEs, but this changed in December 2020.
exp.b: Correct. Since December 2020, S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for all GET, PUT, LIST, and DELETE operations.
exp.c: Incorrect. Strong consistency applies to all operations, not just PUTs.
exp.d: Incorrect. All operations now have strong consistency.

q: How many S3 buckets can you create per AWS account by default?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default is higher than 10.
exp.b: Incorrect. The default is 100, not 50.
exp.c: Correct. By default, you can create up to 100 buckets per AWS account (can be increased to 1000 via service quota request).
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a default limit of 100 buckets per account.

q: What is the maximum number of S3 buckets you can have per AWS account after requesting a quota increase?

exp.a: Incorrect. 100 is the default, not the maximum after increase.
exp.b: Incorrect. The maximum after increase is 1000, not 500.
exp.c: Correct. You can request a service quota increase to have up to 1000 buckets per AWS account.
exp.d: Incorrect. The hard limit is 1000 buckets.

q: Is there a limit on the number of objects you can store in a single S3 bucket?

exp.a: Incorrect. There is no limit on the number of objects per bucket.
exp.b: Incorrect. There is no numerical limit.
exp.c: Correct. You can store an unlimited number of objects in a single S3 bucket.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is no 100,000 object limit.

q: What is the S3 request rate performance for GET/HEAD requests per prefix?

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 supports more than 1,000 GET requests per prefix.
exp.b: Incorrect. 3,500 requests per second is the rate for PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE per prefix.
exp.c: Correct. S3 supports 5,500 GET/HEAD requests per second per prefix.
exp.d: Incorrect. The rate is 5,500, not 10,000.

q: What is the S3 request rate performance for PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE requests per prefix?

exp.a: Incorrect. The rate is higher than 1,000 per second.
exp.b: Correct. S3 supports 3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE requests per second per prefix.
exp.c: Incorrect. 5,500 is the rate for GET/HEAD requests per prefix.
exp.d: Incorrect. The rate is 3,500, not 10,000.

q: Which S3 feature sends notifications when specific events occur on a bucket (e.g., object creation)?

exp.a: Incorrect. Lifecycle Policies transition or expire objects, not send notifications.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Event Notifications can trigger SNS, SQS, Lambda, or EventBridge when events like object creation or deletion occur.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 Analytics provides storage class usage analysis.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 Inventory provides reports of objects and their metadata.

q: Which of the following are valid destinations for S3 Event Notifications? (Choose the best answer)

opts.a: SNS, SQS, Lambda, and Amazon EventBridge

exp.a: Correct. S3 Event Notifications can be sent to SNS, SQS, Lambda functions, and Amazon EventBridge.
exp.b: Incorrect. SQS and EventBridge are also valid destinations.
exp.c: Incorrect. SNS and EventBridge are also valid destinations.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudWatch Alarms are not a direct destination for S3 Event Notifications.

q: What does S3 Inventory provide?

opts.b: A scheduled report listing objects and their metadata in a bucket

exp.a: Incorrect. GuardDuty and CloudTrail handle security alerts.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Inventory generates scheduled (daily or weekly) reports listing objects along with metadata like size, storage class, encryption status, etc.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 does not automatically compress objects.
exp.d: Incorrect. Replication status is available per object, but Inventory provides scheduled bulk reports.

q: What does S3 Storage Lens provide?

opts.b: Organization-wide visibility into S3 usage and activity with metrics and recommendations

exp.a: Incorrect. Encryption management is done via bucket settings and KMS.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide visibility into storage usage, activity trends, and cost optimization recommendations.
exp.c: Incorrect. Lifecycle policies handle storage class transitions.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 does not provide a compression service.

q: What is an S3 Access Point?

opts.b: A named network endpoint with its own access policy to simplify managing access to shared datasets

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudFront provides CDN endpoints, not Access Points.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Access Points are named network endpoints with dedicated access policies, simplifying management for shared buckets with many users/applications.
exp.c: Incorrect. VPN is not related to S3 Access Points.
exp.d: Incorrect. Access Points are for access management, not backup.

q: Which S3 feature allows you to perform large-scale batch operations on existing objects?

exp.a: Incorrect. Lifecycle Policies handle transitions/expirations based on rules.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Batch Operations allows you to perform operations (copy, invoke Lambda, restore, tag, etc.) on billions of objects with a single request.
exp.c: Incorrect. Event Notifications trigger actions on new events.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 Select retrieves subsets of object data.

q: Which type of S3 policy is attached directly to the bucket and uses JSON format?

exp.a: Incorrect. IAM Policies are attached to users, groups, or roles, not directly to buckets.
exp.b: Correct. Bucket Policies are JSON-based policies attached directly to S3 buckets for resource-based access control.
exp.c: Incorrect. ACLs are a legacy access control mechanism and use XML, not JSON.
exp.d: Incorrect. Security Groups are for EC2/VPC, not S3.

q: What is the S3 Block Public Access feature designed to do?

opts.a: Block all access to the bucket including the owner
opts.b: Provide account-level and bucket-level settings to prevent public access regardless of individual policies

exp.a: Incorrect. Block Public Access prevents public access, not all access.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Block Public Access provides settings at account and bucket level to override policies and ACLs that would grant public access.
exp.c: Incorrect. Encryption is handled separately.
exp.d: Incorrect. CRR is not affected by Block Public Access.

q: What is MFA Delete in S3?

opts.a: A feature that requires MFA to create a bucket
opts.b: A feature that requires MFA to permanently delete object versions or change versioning state
opts.c: A feature that requires MFA to upload objects
opts.d: A feature that requires MFA to enable encryption

exp.a: Incorrect. MFA is not required for bucket creation.
exp.b: Correct. MFA Delete requires MFA authentication to permanently delete object versions or to suspend/enable versioning on a bucket.
exp.c: Incorrect. MFA is not required for uploading objects.
exp.d: Incorrect. MFA Delete is about deletion protection, not encryption.

q: Which AWS service can be used with S3 to provide a fully managed file transfer service supporting SFTP, FTPS, and FTP?

exp.a: Incorrect. DataSync is for migrating data between on-premises and AWS, but does not provide SFTP/FTP endpoints.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP, and AS2 endpoints that store data directly in S3.
exp.c: Incorrect. Storage Gateway provides hybrid storage but does not offer managed FTP/SFTP.
exp.d: Incorrect. Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection.

q: What does S3 Requester Pays mean?

opts.a: The bucket owner pays for all requests and data transfer
opts.b: The requester (not the bucket owner) pays for requests and data transfer out
opts.c: AWS pays for all S3 costs
opts.d: Only authenticated users can access the bucket

exp.a: Incorrect. This is the default behavior, not Requester Pays.
exp.b: Correct. With Requester Pays, the requester (authenticated AWS user) pays for request and data transfer costs instead of the bucket owner.
exp.c: Incorrect. AWS does not pay for customer S3 costs.
exp.d: Incorrect. While requesters must be authenticated, the key feature is cost shifting.

q: Which S3 feature enables you to analyze access patterns to determine the optimal storage class?

exp.a: Incorrect. Storage Lens provides broader usage metrics but does not specifically recommend transitions per object group.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Analytics – Storage Class Analysis observes access patterns and provides recommendations on when to transition objects to IA classes.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 Inventory lists objects and metadata but does not analyze access patterns.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 Select retrieves data subsets from objects.

q: What is the purpose of S3 Object Lambda?

opts.a: To automatically compress objects on upload
opts.b: To transform data retrieved from S3 using Lambda functions before returning it to the application
opts.c: To trigger Lambda on object deletion only
opts.d: To encrypt objects with custom algorithms

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 does not automatically compress objects.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Object Lambda allows you to add your own code via Lambda to process/transform data as it is retrieved from S3 (e.g., redact PII, resize images).
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 Event Notifications can trigger Lambda on deletion; Object Lambda transforms GET responses.
exp.d: Incorrect. Encryption is handled by SSE options, not Object Lambda.

q: Which AWS service is commonly placed in front of S3 to cache content globally and reduce latency?

exp.a: Incorrect. Route 53 is a DNS service, not a content caching service.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that caches S3 content at edge locations to reduce latency globally.
exp.c: Incorrect. Global Accelerator optimizes network routing but doesn't cache content.
exp.d: Incorrect. ElastiCache is an in-memory cache for databases, not for S3 content distribution.

q: What is an S3 VPC Endpoint (Gateway Endpoint) used for?

opts.b: To allow private access to S3 from within a VPC without traversing the public internet
opts.c: To speed up S3 uploads using edge locations
opts.d: To encrypt data in transit to S3

exp.a: Incorrect. VPC Endpoints do not make buckets public.
exp.b: Correct. S3 Gateway Endpoints allow EC2 instances and other resources in a VPC to access S3 privately without going over the internet.
exp.c: Incorrect. Transfer Acceleration uses edge locations for upload speed.
exp.d: Incorrect. HTTPS handles encryption in transit.

q: What logging feature records all requests made to an S3 bucket for audit purposes?

exp.a: Correct. S3 Server Access Logging records detailed information about requests made to a bucket, stored in a target bucket.
exp.b: Incorrect. Versioning preserves object versions, not access logs.
exp.c: Incorrect. Lifecycle Policies manage object transitions and expiration.
exp.d: Incorrect. Storage Lens provides aggregate metrics, not per-request logs.

q: When enabling S3 Server Access Logging, where should the logs be stored?

opts.a: In the same bucket being logged
opts.b: In a different bucket in the same region (target/logging bucket)

exp.a: Incorrect. Storing logs in the same bucket can create an infinite logging loop and is not recommended.
exp.b: Correct. Logs should be stored in a separate target bucket (must be in the same AWS Region) to avoid logging loops.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 Server Access Logs are stored in an S3 bucket, not directly in CloudWatch Logs.
exp.d: Incorrect. EBS volumes cannot be configured as a log destination for S3.
